title: Backfill incident_type/subtype from logs pipeline for historical reporting
author: Mei Lin
description:
Context: As part of the Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping rollout, we need baseline reporting for the last ~90 days (and optionally 2 quarters) so we can validate category distribution and SLA compliance by type/owner. Not all historical incidents have incident_type set in incident-bot (or the value is missing due to older bot versions / INT-772). This PR adds an offline backfill job that infers incident_type/subtype from existing logs/annotations (incident-bot events, alert payloads, and a small set of high-signal routing/serving markers) and writes the result into the analytics store used by incident dashboards. This is explicitly not used for live incident routing or gating; it is for historical reporting only.

What this does: (1) Adds a backfill pipeline stage `incident_taxonomy_backfill` that consumes incident timeline events and related alert/log records over a configurable time window. (2) Implements an inference function that maps symptoms/signals to v1 taxonomy categories (e.g., 5xx overload, latency regression, streaming disconnects, routing fallback misbehavior, capacity/fleet shortage, control plane outage, auth/RBAC failure, telemetry blind spot, private connectivity/config). (3) Emits `incident_type`, `incident_subtype`, `inference_source`, and `confidence` to the `analytics.incidents_enriched` table and keeps the original human-entered fields intact (we never overwrite). (4) Adds a CLI entrypoint for one-off runs and a scheduled job definition for the standard “last 90 days” backfill.

Accuracy + caveats (important): This is best-effort classification with known limitations. It is intentionally conservative: when multiple types match or the evidence is weak, it emits incident_type=unknown and a low confidence score. We also preserve contributing signals for audit/debug in logs, but we do not store raw log lines in the analytics output. The mapping is based on an allowlist of v1 types/subtypes to avoid label/cardinality explosion. This should be good enough for aggregate reporting (top categories, trend lines), but not for per-incident root cause analysis.

Signals used (high level): incident-bot fields/tags where present; alert payload fields (service/route, http status family, SLO burn labels); routing fallback_reason enums (from pr-28437) where available; a small set of runtime symptoms (OOM/kv-cache thrash/scheduler stall markers) when they appear as structured log annotations; and control plane error codes for config write failures. The inference prioritizes explicit incident-bot taxonomy when present, then structured alert payload taxonomy when present, then falls back to heuristics.

Testing/validation: Added unit tests for the inference rules and golden fixtures for a few representative incident timelines. Added a dry-run mode that reports distribution by inferred type and % unknown so we can iterate without writing. Ran on staging for 14 days of data: ~71% inferred with >=0.7 confidence, ~19% unknown, ~10% low-confidence inferred (mostly multi-cause capacity+routing incidents). We expect unknown to drop as more historical incidents have explicit taxonomy set via the bot.

Follow-ups: (a) Tune heuristics for multi-cause incidents (primary vs contributing) after taxonomy workshop feedback; (b) add a small manual review UI/workflow to correct a subset of low-confidence inferences; (c) document the intended use (aggregate only) in the dashboards spec and ops guide.

Privacy/security: The enriched table contains only incident identifiers, timestamps, taxonomy fields, and a small set of non-PII structured attributes (service, region, tier). No customer prompts/responses, request bodies, or IP addresses are persisted by this job.
commits: data-pipeline: add incident taxonomy backfill job scaffolding + CLI
taxonomy: implement inference ruleset + confidence scoring
tests: add fixtures + golden tests for inference mapping
docs: add runbook note + operational caveats for backfill
review_conversation:
Allison Grant (Observability): Please confirm we’re not introducing any new high-cardinality labels or writing raw log lines into analytics. Also, can we ensure the output values are strictly the taxonomy allowlist (unknown included)? Mei Lin (author): Confirmed. Output is constrained to `incident_taxonomy_allowlist.py`; unknown is the only fallback. We do not persist raw log lines; the job only reads structured fields and writes taxonomy + a small set of attributes (service, region, tier). Added an explicit schema validation test to fail if an out-of-allowlist value is produced.

Aisha Bello (SLO/SLA dashboards): How will we avoid confusing inferred values with human-entered values in dashboards? We need to be able to filter/compare. Mei Lin: Added `inference_source` (human|alert_payload|heuristic|unknown) and `confidence` to the output. The dashboard query can default to human when present; otherwise use inferred. I also added a note in docs/ops/incident-taxonomy/backfill-job.md.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Multi-cause incidents: if the timeline has both fleet capacity alerts and routing fallback_reason spikes, which wins? Mei Lin: Current priority is (1) human-set taxonomy (if present), (2) control-plane outage/auth failures (more specific), (3) capacity/fleet shortage when we see sustained saturation/provisioning lag without healthy fallback, (4) routing fallback misbehavior when fallback_reason indicates policy/health misrouting and 5xx increases are tied to routing changes. When both match strongly, we emit unknown + low confidence rather than guessing. I added tests for the “capacity then routing” fixture.

Ethan Park (Control plane): Any coupling to control plane internals that could break? Mei Lin: Only uses stable error codes and structured incident annotations already emitted; if absent, the rule doesn’t trigger. No direct reads from control plane DB.

Sergio Costa: Minor: Can we add a dry-run summary output (counts by type + % unknown) to make iterations faster? Mei Lin: Added `--dry-run` and `--print-summary` to CLI; wired into job logs in staging.
release_notes: Internal: Added an offline backfill job to infer incident taxonomy for historical incidents to support reliability reporting. Does not affect live incident routing or customer-facing behavior.
